summary: Story 3 adds an optional String department field to Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest, and an optional department query parameter on GET /api/employees. The human clarified the filter behavior: an omitted parameter returns all employees; a blank or whitespace-only parameter returns HTTP 200 with []; an unknown department returns HTTP 200 with []; matching is case-insensitive and exact. GET by ID and POST without department must keep working as they do now. The feature reuses the existing in-memory EmployeeService with no database or new services, and Swagger/OpenAPI must document the parameter and the updated schemas. Requirements are testable. Human approval of this regenerated handoff is pending.
decisions: approval: pending - the human supplied a clarification of the department-filter behavior but has not approved this regenerated requirements handoff; finishing this handoff does not count as approval.

Human clarification (authoritative, supersedes run-002): missing department parameter returns all employees; blank or whitespace-only department returns HTTP 200 with []; unknown department returns HTTP 200 with []; department matching is case-insensitive exact matching. The run-002 assumption that a blank parameter is treated as omitted and returns all employees is removed.

Current behavior: Employee is a record (id, name, email). CreateEmployeeRequest has (name @NotBlank, email @NotBlank @Email). EmployeeService stores employees in an in-memory LinkedHashMap keyed by id, in insertion order. GET /api/employees takes no parameters and returns every employee.
FR1: Add department (String) to the Employee record and to CreateEmployeeRequest. EmployeeService.create stores request.department() on the new Employee.
FR2: department is optional on POST. It gets no @NotBlank or other new validation, so POST bodies without department still return 201, and department is null in the response.
FR3: GET /api/employees accepts an optional department query parameter (required = false).

FR4: When department is present and not blank, return only employees whose department equals the parameter value ignoring case (case-insensitive exact match, e.g. equalsIgnoreCase). No partial, prefix, or substring matching.
FR5: When the department parameter is omitted entirely, GET /api/employees returns all employees, exactly as it does today.

FR6: When the department parameter is present but blank or whitespace-only (e.g. ?department= or ?department=%20%20), return HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array []. This is distinct from omitting the parameter. (Clarified by the human.)
FR7: When no employee matches a non-blank department, the response is HTTP 200 with an empty JSON array [], not 404.

FR8: GET /api/employees/{id} keeps its current behavior: 200 with Employee, or 404 with ErrorResponse {"error":"Employee not found"}. POST keeps 201 on success and 400 with {"error":"Invalid employee data"} for invalid or malformed input.

FR9: Swagger/OpenAPI documents the optional department query parameter (string, not required) on GET /api/employees, and adds department (type string) to the Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest schemas. The set of paths and operations and the documented response codes stay the same.

FR10: Add focused tests for the department filter (match, case variation, omitted, blank, whitespace-only, unknown) and for POST with and without department, and run the full existing regression suite.
AC1: GET /api/employees?department=IT returns only employees whose department equals IT, ignoring case.
AC2: GET /api/employees?department=it returns results equivalent to AC1.
AC3: GET /api/employees with no department parameter returns all employees.
AC4: GET /api/employees?department= (empty) and GET /api/employees?department=<whitespace only> each return HTTP 200 with [], even when employees exist.
AC5: GET /api/employees?department=<unknown> returns HTTP 200 with [].
AC6: Matching is exact: a partial value (e.g. department=I when an employee has IT) does not match.
AC7: POST without department returns 201 with the same id, name, and email values as before. Existing GET by ID, POST validation, and malformed-JSON tests still pass.
AC8: The OpenAPI document at /v3/api-docs shows the department query parameter as optional and includes department in the Employee and CreateEmployeeRequest schemas. Swagger UI still loads.
AC9: All existing and new tests pass.
Constraint: Keep the implementation minimal and reuse the existing Spring Boot controller/service/record structure. Do not add a database, repository layer, or new services.
Constraint: Do not modify existing Copilot agents, hooks, .github/ customizations, or Story 1/2 evidence under .sdlc/. Make no commits, pushes, or PRs without human approval.
Assumption: Employees whose department is null never match a non-blank department filter.
Assumption: The department value is stored as given, with no case normalization on storage. Only the comparison ignores case.
Assumption: Non-blank filter values are compared as given, without trimming, consistent with exact matching (e.g. ' IT ' does not match 'IT'). Confirm at approval if trimming is wanted.

Risk: Spring binds ?department= to an empty string (not null) when required = false, so the implementation must distinguish null (omitted, return all) from blank (return []); a default value on the parameter would break this distinction.

Risk: OpenApiDocumentationTests asserts exact property sets for Employee {id, name, email} and CreateEmployeeRequest {name, email}. Those assertions must change to include department; this is an expected documentation change, not a regression.

Risk: Employee JSON responses gain a department property, which is null when not supplied. Existing clients that strictly reject unknown fields could be affected. This is acceptable as an additive change, and existing tests only check specific fields.
Risk: Adding a field changes the record's canonical constructor. Every call site of new Employee(...) and every test that builds requests must be updated consistently.
